purpose: Dimethyl fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), helping to reduce the number of flare-ups and slow down disability progression. It is also used to treat moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in some countries. Basically, it helps calm down an overactive immune system that is attacking your body.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks your own nerve cells or skin. Dimethyl fumarate works by activating a natural protective pathway in your body called Nrf2, which helps reduce inflammation and protects cells from damage. Think of it like turning on your body's own built-in shield against the immune system going haywire.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are flushing (feeling hot, red, or tingly in your face and body), stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, and stomach pain. These effects are often worse when you first start the medication and usually improve over time. Taking it with food can help reduce these symptoms.
warnings: This medication can lower your white blood cell count, which means your body may have a harder time fighting infections, so your doctor will do regular blood tests to monitor this. In rare cases, it has been linked to a serious brain infection called PML, especially if your white blood cell count stays very low. Do not take it if you are allergic to dimethyl fumarate, and tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
typical_dosing: For MS (Tecfidera), you usually start with a lower dose of 120 mg twice a day for the first month, then increase to the full dose of 240 mg twice a day. Always take it with food to help reduce stomach and flushing side effects. Follow your doctor's instructions exactly and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
